items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Anyway, at that time she was very normal and anxious for me to know her stuff. And went over it with her and everything.

ctx.x: Yeah, she became a purist -- modernist after she got discovered. This music was not her bag. She was now into 'Little Boy Blue' or something, I forgot. These tunes that the modernists -- if you sing them, you're hip. She got into that.

Anyway, at that time she was very normal and anxious for me to know her stuff. And went over it with her and everything. Four days, I fitted right in the band. But I told them I didn't want to stay, because I says, I can't join you because you're going to get up and move. And I'm not travelling that much. I had three offers from Louis Armstrong to join him.

And I have to think that I have Barney Bigard to thank for it. And the band -- whoever -- Frenchie, Frenchie looked at me and says, you belong in that scene. See, Earl had left, and before Joe Sullivan came in, they wanted me. And after Joe Sullivan came in they wanted me. So this is pre-Napoleon.
